## 28ad783a6a98

**A1 — Reproduced exact-override contract defect, not incorrect labels for the generated scene.** Generator SHA256 `95f54757a4ca6678f428b2b16b6626091eef245650bf9f32d85875753a7876a2`; rule hash `de08015bfb28`, complete canonical source SHA256 `de08015bfb282947470ce41bc56a6c042ae2486ce7c21ced9fc64beb25168787`.

The generator depicts two transformations and requests their composition on a fifth panel. It advertises exact `first_transform` and `second_transform` controls. Explicit inverse pairs are silently replaced in order to avoid a composite identity. All motifs in this probe have unique transform observations, so this is not an ambiguous symmetric-motif attribution.

Reproduction: seed 0, sample index 0, overrides `first_transform="r1", second_transform="r3"`. The first observed transform is r1 but the second is atr, not r3. The requested composition is identity on the query panel; the actual Racket output differs because the generated second demonstration was rewritten. Full witness: `checks/audits/28ad783a6a98-counterexample.json`. Input 4x24, output 4x4, target validator errors `[]`, documented generator domain true. An identity composition is NOT raw input-output equality: the task still extracts a panel from a larger input.

Matrix: seeds 0..9, sample index 0, all 7x7 advertised nonidentity D4-transform pairs, 490 generated scenes. 70/490 mismatch their requested exact controls; all 70 are the inverse-composition cases and all 70 were checked through actual canonical Racket. All 490 pass the target validator. Every mismatch is listed in `checks/audits/report.json`; the first full witness is retained separately. The comparator output means “the composition explicitly requested by the caller,” not an alternative correct label for the rewritten panels.

Suggested owner repair: honor inverse combinations, or explicitly reject/document incompatibility rather than changing a requested exact value. No code change here. No exhaustive arbitrary motifs/seeds or model-learning claim.

## 28ad783a6a98

**Finding A2 — reproduced exact-override rewrite.** Assigned generator SHA-256
`95f54757a4ca6678f428b2b16b6626091eef245650bf9f32d85875753a7876a2`
advertises `first_transform` and `second_transform` as exact controls, but
`generate()` silently replaces the second transform whenever the requested
composition leaves panel X unchanged. The generated lesson remains internally
consistent with the replacement and passes `self_check`, so downstream code can
believe the requested curriculum axis was honored when it was not.

The retained matrix requested all 49 transform pairs for seeds 0–9 at sample
index 0: 70/490 draws (14.2857%) encoded a different second transform, with
0/490 `self_check` failures. There were 420 unique inputs because each of the
seven inverse-pair requests per seed collapsed onto another realized pair.
The minimal retained witness requests `r1` then `r3` at seed 0. Its panels encode
`r1` then `atr`; the requested inverse pair would return X unchanged, while the
canonical Racket authority (`de08015bfb28`) returns the non-identity output
implied by the rewritten panels. Thus the rule output is correct for the pixels,
but the advertised exact-control contract is false.

The official override stage independently failed and also reported an accepted
unknown key, inert/singleton axes, and diagnostic combinations that ignore
controls. The hash-bound witness contains the generated input, validator result,
actual Racket output, requested rival output, commands, and hashes in
`checks/audits/28ad783a6a98/counterexample.json`; the complete matrix is
`checks/audits/28ad783a6a98/override_matrix.json`, and the supported apply record
is `checks/audits/28ad783a6a98/racket.json`. The reusable audit-only reproducer is
`checks/audits/reproduce_exact_transform_overrides.py`. I did not edit this audit
target.

Requested exact second_transform=r3 silently changes to atr when requested composition is identity; emitted panels uniquely establish the rewrite and actual Racket matches emitted composition. Validator passes. Exact-control defect, not bad reference label. ## 28ad783a6a98

**Reproduced defect — an advertised exact transform override is silently rewritten.** On generator SHA-256 `95f54757a4ca6678f428b2b16b6626091eef245650bf9f32d85875753a7876a2`, `seed=0`, `sample_index=0`, `difficulty=medium`, and exact overrides `first_transform=r1`, `second_transform=r3`, the emitted panels uniquely show `r1` followed by `atr`, not the requested `r3`. The requested `r1∘r3` composition is identity on panel X, and `generate()` replaces `t2` after `draw_choice`; this makes a supposedly exact curriculum control non-exact. The input passes `self_check` with `[]`, so validation does not expose the rewrite. The selected Racket authority (`de08015bfb28`) produces the observed-composition output and differs from the requested-composition output; this is an override-contract defect, not a bad label for the scene actually emitted.

Fresh reproducer and source-bound evidence: `checks/audit/28ad783a6a98/reproduce.py`, `checks/audit/28ad783a6a98/counterexample.json`, `checks/audit/28ad783a6a98/input.json`, and `checks/audit/28ad783a6a98/racket.json`. The input is in the documented generator domain and was produced through the advertised overrides. I did not modify this audit-only target.

triage.reason: Both unchanged-source peer findings explicitly unresolved. A successful main-task repair does not clear these or older audits.
